mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate indicates tighter monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces consumer and business spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases when FEDFUNDS exceeds 5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate signals a strong labor market, increasing consumer confidence and spending, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 has negative 20-day returns in more than 30% of cases when UNRATE is below 4%, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Strong real personal consumption expenditures indicate robust demand, driving economic growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the Rank IC for RSAFS and S&P 500 is below 0.03 over a 3-year window, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production suggests economic expansion, boosting corporate earnings and leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of cases when INDPRO rises, the hypothesis is invalid.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in non-farm payroll employment indicates a strong labor market, increasing economic activity and leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 has negative 20-day returns in more than 30% of cases when PAYEMS grows, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate is low and the federal funds rate is high, it indicates a tight labor market with high interest rates, negatively impacting the S&P 500 over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of triggered cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth coupled with high CPI suggests inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 has positive 60-day returns in more than 30% of triggered cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, high federal funds rates increase borrowing costs, reducing corporate profitability and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases when FEDFUNDS is above 5%, the hypothesis is rejected.
